holidays.name: Create a Vacuum Day
holidays.description: A day that invites you to think about nothing at all. Or about the physics of empty space. Or about the machine that sucks crumbs out of your couch. Pick your favorite kind of void and enjoy it.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is popular with science fans and anyone who enjoys a good pun.
holidays.funFact: In 1654, German scientist Otto von Guericke pumped the air out of two joined copper hemispheres. Teams of horses could not pull them apart, which made the power of a vacuum clear to everyone watching.

holidays.name: National Stuffed Mushroom Day
holidays.description: A salute to the bite-sized party appetizer. Mushroom caps get packed with breadcrumbs, cheese, garlic, herbs, sausage, or crab, then baked until golden. Make a batch and see how fast the plate empties.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It is a favorite of appetizer lovers everywhere.
holidays.funFact: Mushrooms are not plants. They belong to the fungi kingdom, which makes them closer relatives of animals than of the tomatoes and herbs you might stuff them with.

holidays.name: National Thank a Mail Carrier Day
holidays.description: A day to say thanks to the people who bring your packages, bills, and birthday cards in every kind of weather. A wave, a note, or a cold drink left on the porch will make their day.
holidays.origin: This is an annual appreciation observance that encourages people to recognize their local letter carriers.
holidays.funFact: The famous line about neither snow nor rain stopping couriers is carved on New York City's main post office building. It is not an official U.S. Postal Service motto. The words are adapted from the ancient Greek historian Herodotus, who was describing Persian messengers.
